title: Radical Candor
author: Kim Scott
blurb: Kim Scott, who led teams at Google and Apple, argues that the best bosses do two things at once. They care personally about the people who work for them, and they challenge those people directly. Put those two dimensions on a grid and you get four ways of managing. Radical Candor sits where both are high. Ruinous Empathy is caring without challenging. Obnoxious Aggression is challenging without caring. Manipulative Insincerity is neither. Scott shows how to build candid relationships by asking for criticism before giving it, and by offering praise and criticism that is humble, helpful, immediate and in person. She also shows how to understand what motivates each person, whether they want rapid growth or steady excellence. She also lays out a practical process for getting things done as a team. The result is a guide to being a demanding boss without losing your humanity.

lessons.t: The Feedback That Changed Her Career
lessons.b: When Sheryl Sandberg bluntly told Scott she sounded unprepared because she kept saying um, Scott learned that real caring means telling people what they need to hear.
